sections.title: 1.1 Purpose
sections.text_preview: This document details the software requirements specification for the PDF Split and Merge v2.1.0 open source project. It will later be used as a base for the extension of the existing software itself.

sections.title: 1.2 Document Conventions
sections.text_preview: PDF Split and Merge was created prior to this document, so all requirements stated here are already satisfied. It is very important to update this document with every future requirement and clarify it

sections.title: 1.3 Intended Audience and Reading Suggestions
sections.text_preview:
This Software Requirements document is intended for:

Developers who can review project’s capabilities and more easily understand where their efforts should be targeted to improve or add more features

sections.title: 1.4 Project Scope

sections.title: 1.5 References
sections.text_preview:
The official website of the project contains a brief description of the project, screenshots, links, FAQ’s and a blog with all the news of the project: http://www.pdfsam.org/

sections.title: 2.1 Product Perspective
sections.text_preview: PDF Split and Merge is a multi functional tool for manipulating pdf files. It is free and open source with a GNU General Public License (GPL). Although there are many programs for viewing pdfs, there

sections.title: 2.2 Product Features
sections.text_preview:
The basic version provides:

− Splitting pdf documents (into chapters, single pages, etc).

− Merging many pdf documents or subsections of them.

− Extract section from a pdf document in a single pdf

sections.title: 2.3 User Classes and Characteristics
sections.text_preview:
This project refers to several types of users of any computer system. However, this project is meant to be used by two major user classes:

1. General users who can use the software to cover specific

sections.title: 2.4 Operating Environment
sections.text_preview:
PDFsam is platform independent and it runs on every platform where a Java Virtual Machine is available (requires a JVM version 1.6 or higher).

It has been tested on:

− Microsoft Windows

− GNU/Linux

sections.title: 2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints
sections.text_preview: PDFsam is platform independent and is written in Java. Its user interface is written with Java Swing, so anyone who wishes to work on further development of PDFsam has to know this programming languag

sections.title: 2.6 User Documentation
sections.text_preview:
User documentation components are available on project’s official website:

http://www.pdfsam.org/ (in the Resources section)

Refer to section 1.5 of this document for further information.

sections.title: 2.7 Assumptions and Dependencies
sections.text_preview: A working Java Runtime Environment version 1.6 or above is necessary.
